scenario: 45 分钟的 AI coding 面试，方案已在前 10 分钟定好，剩下时间全程共享屏幕写代码。
scenario_en: It's a 45-minute AI coding interview; the approach was settled in the first ten minutes, and the rest is live coding on a shared screen.
q: AI coding 面试进入执行阶段后，面试官最常评估的不是你打字多快，而是什么？
q_en: Once an AI coding interview reaches execution, what are interviewers really evaluating?
options: 你是否持续提示、审阅并掌控 AI 的输出
你是否让 AI 独自决定架构方案
你是否尽量避免运行和验证代码
你是否写出全场最长的一段提示
options_en: Whether you keep prompting, reviewing, and steering the AI's output.
Whether you let the AI decide the architecture entirely on its own.
Whether you avoid running and verifying the code.
Whether you write the single longest prompt in the room.
why: 执行阶段考核的是你能否按计划驱动 AI、审阅它的产出并持续掌控方向，而不是把决策权交给模型。
why_en: During execution, interviewers watch whether you keep driving, reviewing, and steering the AI instead of handing it the decisions.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Plan[Plan] --> Prompt[Prompt AI]
  Prompt --> Review[Review output]
  Review --> Run[Run code]
  Run --> Adjust[Adjust]
  Adjust --> Prompt
optionExplanations: 这正是评分点：你全程在提示、审阅、纠偏，AI 只是执行你的判断。
误解：把方案决策权交给 AI，面试官反而看不到你自己的工程判断。
误解：省掉运行验证不是效率，是把错误留到后面一次性爆发。
误解：提示字数不是评分维度，提示是否精确锁定约束才是。
optionExplanations_en: Exactly the scoring signal — you're prompting, reviewing, and correcting course the whole time.
Misconception: handing the whole architecture decision to the AI hides your own engineering judgment from the interviewer.
Misconception: skipping verification isn't efficiency, it just lets errors pile up until they explode at once.
Misconception: prompt length isn't the scoring axis — precisely naming constraints is.

scenario: 面试限时 40 分钟实现前缀搜索，你已想清用什么数据结构，但没时间逐行手写实现。
scenario_en: You have 40 minutes to build prefix search. You already know which data structure you want, but no time to hand-write every line.
q: 写 AI 提示时，粒度的“甜点区”具体是什么？
q_en: What is the sweet spot for prompt granularity when coding with AI?
options: 只给原始题目，让 AI 自己决定所有方案
明确要做什么和怎么做，但让 AI 处理语法和惯用写法
逐行规定变量名和代码格式
完全不用 AI
options_en: Hand over the raw problem and let the AI pick the whole approach.
State the what and how clearly, but let the AI handle syntax and idioms.
Dictate variable names and formatting line by line.
Skip the AI entirely.
why: 太泛会让 AI 接管决策，太细又变成隔着 AI 手写代码；合适粒度是你定策略、AI 写实现。
why_en: The sweet spot is stating the what and how clearly while letting the AI handle syntax and idiomatic implementation.
tradeoff: 约束够用 vs 微管理成本 —— 提示太泛让 AI 接管决策，提示太细就变成隔着 AI 手写代码。
optionExplanations: 题目原样甩给 AI 时，你等于把方案选择权让出去，面试官看不到你的判断。
把 what/how 钉死、语法交给 AI，是省时间又保住判断权的甜点区。
连变量名都亲自口述，等于隔着 AI 手写，速度反而不如自己直接打字。
完全不用工具能保留全部判断，但放弃了它能省下的实现时间。
optionExplanations_en: Handing over the raw problem lets the AI pick the whole approach, so the interviewer never sees your call.
Pinning down the what and how while leaving syntax to the AI is the sweet spot — fast and still your judgment.
Dictating even variable names turns the AI into a typing proxy, slower than just typing it yourself.
Skipping the AI keeps every decision yours, but gives up the implementation speed it could have offered.

scenario: 你要实现前缀搜索，并已经决定使用 trie（前缀树），每个节点要保存字符和是否为单词结尾。
scenario_en: You need prefix search and have already chosen a trie, where each node stores a character and an end-of-word flag.
q: 哪条提示最符合推荐的提示粒度？
q_en: Which prompt best matches the recommended level of granularity?
options: 不给任何设计信息，只说一句“写点代码把前缀搜索功能实现掉，随便怎么做”，没有提数据结构
trie 支持 insert 和 prefix search，节点存字符、子节点和结束标记
先声明一个变量 a，再写好 for 循环，然后要求 AI 逐行照我口述的每一句代码往下写
需求只是新增一个前缀搜索方法，却要求 AI 顺带把整个项目重写成更好的分层架构
options_en: Give zero design detail — just say 'write some code for prefix search, any way you like,' naming no data structure.
A trie supporting insert and prefix search, each node storing a character, its children, and an end-of-word marker.
Declare a variable, write out a for loop, then have the AI type each line exactly as I dictate it, one by one.
Even though you only need one new method, ask the AI to rewrite the whole project into a better layered architecture.
why: 这条提示锁定了数据结构和节点字段，但把语法实现留给 AI，正好落在推荐的提示粒度上。
why_en: This prompt fixes the data structure and node fields while leaving syntax to the AI, landing right in the recommended granularity.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是改一行判断条件，自己直接写通常比提示 AI 更快。
tradeoff: 锁定方案与字段 vs 逐行口述实现 —— 提示到数据结构层就够，细到变量名就是隔着 AI 手写。
codeSample:
Implement a trie that supports insert(word) and searchByPrefix(prefix).
Each TrieNode stores: character, children map, isEndOfWord boolean.
Fit it into the existing Dictionary class; keep it concise.
optionDiagrams:
flowchart LR
  Task[Raw task] --> AI[AI decides]
  AI --> Drift[Drift risk]

flowchart LR
  You[Trie decision] --> AI[Implement methods]
  AI --> Fit[Code fits plan]

flowchart LR
  You[Line orders] --> AI[Typing proxy]
  AI --> Slow[Slow loop]

flowchart LR
  Scope[Small feature] --> Rewrite[Rewrite project]
  Rewrite --> Risk[Huge risk]

termDefinitions.meaning: 前缀树，一种按字符逐层存储字符串前缀的数据结构，适合前缀搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trie is a prefix tree that stores strings character by character to make prefix search fast.

termDefinitions.meaning: trie 里的单个节点，通常保存一个字符、子节点集合和是否为单词结尾的标记。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TrieNode is a single node in a trie holding a character, its children, and an end-of-word flag.

termDefinitions.meaning: trie 节点上的布尔标记，标记从根到此节点的路径是否恰好是一个完整单词。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: isEndOfWord is a boolean flag on a trie node marking whether the path from the root to this node spells a complete word.

optionExplanations: 不给结构信息时，AI 可能选哈希表而不是你已经定好的 trie。
锁定数据结构和字段、放开语法细节，正落在推荐的提示粒度上。
口述到每一句代码，等于隔着 AI 手写，比自己直接实现还慢。
题目只要一个方法，却引导 AI 做架构级重写，范围严重失控。
optionExplanations_en: Without any structure hint, the AI might reach for a hash map instead of the trie you already chose.
Fixing the data structure and fields while leaving syntax open lands exactly in the recommended granularity.
Dictating every line turns the AI into a typing proxy, slower than just writing it yourself.
The task only needs one method, but this steers the AI into an architecture-level rewrite — scope spirals.

scenario: 你要让 AI 实现一个复杂状态机（用状态和转移规则描述行为的模型），转移规则多且容易出错。
scenario_en: You need the AI to implement a complex state machine with many transition rules and easy-to-miss edge cases.
q: 这类任务的提示应该偏向什么风格？
q_en: What prompt style fits this kind of task?
options: 只说“实现状态机”
明确状态、转移、约束和边界行为
让 AI 自己发明状态
不要告诉 AI 任何现有接口
options_en: Just say 'implement a state machine.'
Spell out the states, transitions, constraints, and edge behavior.
Let the AI invent its own states.
Withhold every existing interface from the AI.
why: 复杂逻辑需要更具体的方向，避免 AI 用看似合理但不符合题意的状态设计。
why_en: Tricky logic needs precise states, transitions, constraints, and edge behavior so the AI implements what you actually intend.
whenOtherWins: 如果是重复样板代码，如类似的 API handler，可以用更短的提示再仔细验证。
tradeoff: 具体约束换正确率 vs 省提示时间 —— 逻辑越容易出错，越要提前说清状态和转移。

termDefinitions.meaning: 用有限个状态和转移规则描述系统行为的模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A state machine models behavior as a fixed set of states with rules for transitioning between them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用程序编程接口，模块之间约定好的调用方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is an Application Programming Interface, the agreed-upon way one piece of code calls another.

optionExplanations: 只给任务名不给约束，转移规则的边界情况多半会被漏掉。
状态、转移、边界都写清楚，AI 落地的状态机才会贴合你设计的规则。
状态设计权本该是你的判断，交给 AI 发明容易看似合理却偏离题意。
故意扣住现有接口只会让实现和代码库对不上，之后还要返工。
optionExplanations_en: Naming the task alone with no constraints usually means edge-case transitions get missed.
Spelling out states, transitions, and edges keeps the AI's machine matching the rules you designed.
State design should be your call — letting the AI invent its own can look plausible yet miss the intent.
Deliberately withholding the existing interfaces just makes the result clash with the codebase later.

scenario: 你需要生成五个几乎相同的 API endpoint handler（接收请求并返回响应的处理函数），项目里这种模式已经很标准。
scenario_en: You need five nearly identical API endpoint handlers, and this project already has a clear handler pattern.
q: 面对这批重复 handler，最合理的 AI 用法是什么？
q_en: What is the most reasonable way to use AI for these repetitive handlers?
options: 给短提示让 AI 生成样板，再验证是否遵守既有模式
逐行手写所有重复代码来证明打字能力
让 AI 顺带重新设计整个 API 层
生成之后跳过验证，因为样板一定正确
options_en: Give a short prompt, let the AI generate the boilerplate, then verify it follows the existing pattern.
Hand-write every repetitive line of code to prove your typing skill.
Have the AI redesign the entire API layer while it's at it.
Skip verification after generating, because boilerplate is always correct.
why: AI 很适合处理可验证的重复体力活，你仍要检查它是否照着项目模式写。
why_en: AI is useful for repetitive boilerplate that is easy to verify, as long as you still review it against the local pattern.
whenOtherWins: 如果 handler 里包含关键鉴权或事务边界，提示要更精确，不能只靠模板感生成。
tradeoff: 省时间 vs 验证成本 —— 样板交给 AI 换取速度，但你仍要核对它是否照抄了项目既有模式。
codeSample:
Generate 5 endpoint handlers: GET /orders/{id}, POST /orders, ...
Follow the existing handler pattern in OrderController exactly.
Keep error handling and response shape identical to current handlers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用程序编程接口，模块之间约定好的调用方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is an Application Programming Interface, the agreed-upon way one piece of code calls another.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理某个 API 路径请求、返回响应的函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An endpoint handler is the function that processes requests to a specific API route and returns a response.

termDefinitions.meaning: 项目里高度重复、模式固定的样板代码，比如相似的 API handler。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Boilerplate is highly repetitive, pattern-following code such as near-identical API handlers.

optionExplanations: 体量交给 AI、你负责核对模式一致性，是这类重复活的最优分工。
五个 handler 全部手打，花的时间远超 AI 方案却没有额外收益。
任务只是加 handler，让 AI 顺带重设计整层 API，范围失控。
样板也可能抄错字段或漏掉鉴权，不查一遍风险照样放行。
optionExplanations_en: Handing the volume to the AI while you check pattern consistency is the right split for this kind of repetition.
Hand-typing all five handlers takes far longer than the AI path with no extra benefit.
The task only needed handlers, and letting the AI redesign the whole layer lets scope spiral.
Boilerplate can still copy a field wrong or drop an auth check — skipping review lets that slip through.

q: 补全控制 AI 输出长度的原因：
q_en: Complete the reason for keeping AI output concise:
text: 面试里要让 AI 输出{{简洁}}，因为每一行额外代码都需要你{{审阅}}并可能被要求{{解释}}。
why: 冗长输出会增加理解、验证和辩护成本，常常比它节省的打字时间更贵。
why_en: Concise AI output matters because every extra line must be reviewed and potentially defended.

scenario: 完成代码取向（先读懂项目结构再动手）后，你知道项目已有 Dictionary 类和 TrieNode 结构，需要新增前缀搜索。
scenario_en: After orienting to the codebase, you know it already has a Dictionary class and TrieNode structure, and you need prefix search.
q: 哪条提示最可能产出贴合代码库的代码？
q_en: Which prompt is most likely to produce code that fits this codebase?
options: 不提任何类名，只笼统地说要写一个自动补全功能，别的都不管
给 Dictionary 添加 searchByPrefix，复用现有 TrieNode，返回列表
不管现有结构，让 AI 生成一个全新的 AutocompleteService 类和一套新节点结构
不管代码库现状是什么样子，随便挑一种当下最快能跑起来的写法就行
options_en: Name no existing class at all, just vaguely ask for an autocomplete feature and leave everything else unsaid.
Add searchByPrefix to Dictionary, reusing the existing TrieNode, and return a list of matches.
Ignore the existing structure and have the AI generate a brand-new AutocompleteService class with its own node structure.
Ignore whatever the codebase already looks like and pick whichever approach gets something running fastest right now.
why: 使用真实类名、方法名和数据结构会把 AI 限定在现有架构内，也向面试官展示你读懂了代码。
why_en: Using actual class names, method signatures, and data structures keeps the AI aligned with the existing architecture.
whenOtherWins: 如果现有结构确实不支持需求，应先说明缺口，再设计最小扩展。
tradeoff: 贴合现有架构 vs 生成速度 —— 引用真实类名换来能直接拼进代码库的输出，但提示要多打几个词。
codeSample:
Add searchByPrefix(String prefix) to the Dictionary class.
Reuse the existing TrieNode structure; do not create a new node type.
Return List<String> of all words matching the prefix.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Names[Real class names] --> Bound[Bound AI to repo]
  Bound --> Reuse[Reuse structures]
  Reuse --> Fit[Local fit]

termDefinitions.meaning: trie 里的单个节点，通常保存一个字符、子节点集合和是否为单词结尾的标记。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TrieNode is a single node in a trie holding a character, its children, and an end-of-word flag.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试里指开始写代码前先读懂项目结构、类和方法的阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Orientation is the phase before coding where you read and understand the project’s classes and structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种参数化的字符串列表类型，常见于 Java/Kotlin 风格签名。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: List<String> is a parameterized list-of-strings type common in Java- or Kotlin-style method signatures.

optionExplanations: 缺代码库词汇时，AI 只能猜结构，很容易和 Dictionary/TrieNode 脱节。
点名真实类和真实返回类型，把改动直接钉在现有架构里，改动面最小。
另起一套结构而不是复用 TrieNode，等于制造一份重复且难维护的代码。
只求先跑起来，短期能过但很可能和现有命名、类型冲突，后续要返工。
optionExplanations_en: Without codebase vocabulary, the AI can only guess the shape, likely disconnected from Dictionary/TrieNode.
Naming the real class and return type pins the change straight into the existing architecture with minimal surface.
Building a parallel structure instead of reusing TrieNode just creates a duplicate that's hard to maintain.
Optimizing for whatever runs first may pass today but likely clashes with existing naming and types later.

scenario: 面试仓库里已有 Dictionary 类和一套现成接口，要求新功能复用它们而不是另起一套。
scenario_en: The interview repo already has a Dictionary class and a set of interfaces, and the new feature is supposed to reuse them rather than start fresh.
q: 在提示中引用代码库具体词汇有什么好处？（多选）
q_en: What are the benefits of using codebase-specific vocabulary in prompts? (Select all that apply.)
options: AI 更可能复用已有接口和数据结构
输出更容易融入现有架构
面试官能看到你完成了取向
可以完全不用审阅输出
options_en: The AI is more likely to reuse existing interfaces and data structures.
The output fits the existing architecture more naturally.
The interviewer can see that you actually did the orientation step.
You can skip reviewing the output entirely.
why: 具体词汇改善生成质量并展示上下文理解，但不能替代你对结果的验证。
why_en: Codebase-specific vocabulary improves fit and demonstrates understanding, but it does not remove the need to review.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试里指开始写代码前先读懂项目结构、类和方法的阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Orientation is the phase before coding where you read and understand the project’s classes and structure.

optionExplanations: 挡住的风险：AI 凭空重新发明一套接口，之后要花时间对齐。
减掉的压力：合并代码时不用再手动理顺架构冲突。
带来的信号：用词本身就让面试官看到你读懂了项目结构。
误解：具体词汇改善生成质量，但审阅这一步不能被它替代。
optionExplanations_en: Risk it blocks: the AI reinventing its own interface from scratch, which you'd later have to reconcile.
Pressure it relieves: less manual work untangling architecture conflicts when merging the result.
Signal it sends: your word choice alone shows the interviewer you actually did the orientation step.
Misconception: specific vocabulary improves generation quality, but it never replaces the review step.

scenario: 你发现只需要改一个变量名或一行条件判断，自己 30 秒能完成。
scenario_en: The change is just a variable rename or a one-line condition, and you can do it yourself in 30 seconds.
q: 这类小改动，最好的选择是什么？
q_en: What is the best choice for this tiny change?
options: 直接自己改
让 AI 生成完整补丁
先让 AI 解释变量名历史
暂停等待面试官指示
options_en: Just make the change yourself.
Ask the AI to generate a full patch.
Ask the AI to first explain the variable's history.
Pause and wait for the interviewer to tell you what to do.
why: 小修小改提示 AI 往往更慢，也会显得你离开 AI 就无法写代码。
why_en: For a tiny change you can make in seconds, writing it yourself is faster and shows you are not dependent on AI.
whenOtherWins: 如果小改牵涉多个文件或不确定副作用，可以请 AI 辅助定位影响面。
tradeoff: 自己改的速度 vs 提示 AI 的往返成本 —— 30 秒能搞定的事，提示往返通常更慢还更显得依赖 AI。
optionExplanations: 这是最快的选择：改一行判断，自己动手比写提示还省时间。
误解：为一行改动走完整提示流程，写提示、等结果的时间比手改还长。
误解：历史背景跟这一行改动无关，多问一步纯属绕路。
误解：一行小改不需要等指示，暴露的是对 AI 的依赖而非独立判断。
optionExplanations_en: The fastest call — fixing one condition by hand beats writing and waiting on a prompt.
Misconception: running a full prompt loop for a one-line change costs more time than just typing it.
Misconception: variable history has nothing to do with this edit — it's an unnecessary detour.
Misconception: a one-line fix needs no green light — waiting here signals AI dependency, not judgment.

scenario: 某段标准数据结构实现你知道方案正确，但手写要五分钟，AI 十秒可生成且容易测试。
scenario_en: You already know the standard data-structure approach is correct, but it takes five minutes to type and ten seconds for AI to generate.
q: 这类工作更适合谁来做？
q_en: Who should do this kind of work?
options: 让 AI 生成，你负责方向和验证
永远手写，避免使用 AI
让 AI 决定数据结构
跳过测试直接继续
options_en: Let the AI generate it while you own the direction and verification.
Always hand-write it and avoid AI entirely.
Let the AI decide which data structure to use.
Skip testing and move straight on.
why: AI 适合体量大、正确性可验证的实现工作；关键是方案仍由你选择。
why_en: Use AI for high-volume implementation that is easy to verify while keeping the design decision yourself.
whenOtherWins: 如果难点是算法选择或边界推理，应先自己想清楚再让 AI 实现。
tradeoff: 生成速度 vs 决策归属 —— AI 承担打字体量，但数据结构的选择仍必须是你的判断。
optionExplanations: 十秒拿到已知正确的实现，省下的五分钟能用在更难的部分。
误解：拒绝工具反而在已验证的体力活上浪费掉本可以省下的时间。
误解：数据结构的选择该是你的判断，交给 AI 后错的结构会在边界情况炸掉。
误解：跳过测试等于放弃确认正确性，哪怕方案本身没问题。
optionExplanations_en: Ten seconds for an implementation you already know is correct frees five minutes for the harder part.
Misconception: refusing the tool wastes time on grunt work that's already known to be verifiable.
Misconception: the structure choice should be yours — a wrong AI pick can break on edge cases later.
Misconception: skipping tests means giving up on confirming correctness, even for a known-good approach.

q: 补全 AI 使用原则：
q_en: Complete the principle for using AI during execution:
text: 把 AI 用在{{体量}}上，把自己用在{{判断}}上；AI 可以写得快，但方案选择和取舍要由你负责。
why: 面试要评估你的工程判断，而不是你把模型输出转发到代码库的速度。
why_en: Use AI for volume and yourself for judgment, because the interview evaluates your engineering decisions.
tradeoff: AI 出体量 vs 你出判断 —— 生成速度换不来方案责任，选择和取舍必须你来担。

scenario: 面试还剩 25 分钟，你打算连做三次生成把整个功能写完，最后一次性跑测试。
scenario_en: With 25 minutes left you plan to stack three generations to finish the whole feature, then run the tests once at the end.
q: 为什么不要连续堆叠多次 AI 生成后才第一次运行代码？
q_en: Why should you not stack several AI generations before running the code for the first time?
options: AI 会因为堆叠生成太多次而直接拒绝继续输出
多个局部正确的改动可能互相冲突，最后形成级联错误
运行代码这个动作本身会降低面试评分
面试规则规定测试只能放在最后运行
options_en: The AI will simply refuse to keep generating once you stack too many rounds.
Several locally-correct changes can conflict and surface as one cascading failure.
The act of running the code itself is what lowers your interview score.
Interview rules dictate that tests can only be run at the very end.
why: 每次有意义生成后运行能把错误隔离在最近一步，避免最后同时面对多处冲突。
why_en: Running after each meaningful generation isolates failures to the latest change instead of creating a cascade.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Gen1[Generate step 1] --> Gen2[Generate step 2]
  Gen2 --> Gen3[Generate step 3]
  Gen3 --> Fail[Mixed failure]
  Run[Run each step] -.-> Isolate[Small failure]

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个局部改动叠加后互相冲突，在最后一次运行时集中爆发的一串错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cascading errors happen when several stacked changes conflict and surface together the first time you finally run the code.

optionExplanations: 误解：AI 不会因为堆叠生成次数就拒绝工作，问题不出在它身上。
每步都局部正确，攒到最后一次运行时，冲突会同时爆发难以定位。
误解：运行验证是加分习惯，不是拉低分数的动作。
误解：测试应该跟着每一步走，攒到最后只会让早期错误被掩盖。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: the AI doesn't refuse to work just because generations pile up — that's not the mechanism.
Each step looks locally fine, but stacking them means the final run has to untangle several conflicts at once.
Misconception: running code to verify is a plus habit, not something that costs you points.
Misconception: tests should track each step — saving them for the end just masks earlier errors.

q: 把增量执行循环排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the incremental execution loop in the correct order:
steps: 让 AI 完成一个明确小步骤
确认通过后进入下一步
why: 核心原则是每个有意义变更后马上验证，有问题先修，不在破损代码上继续叠新功能。
why_en: The loop is: generate one clear step, run checks, fix any breakage, then move on.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Prompt[Prompt one change] --> Review[Review diff]
  Review --> Run[Run tests]
  Run --> Decide{Pass?}
  Decide -->|yes| Next[Next step]
  Decide -->|no| Fix[Fix latest step]
  Fix --> Run

scenario: 面试题明确要求复用团队已有的 LRU 缓存工具类，AI 每次却给出标准教科书实现。
scenario_en: The problem explicitly says to reuse the team's existing LRU cache helper, but the AI keeps handing you the standard textbook implementation.
q: AI 的“训练数据偏置”（更容易给出训练语料里最常见的解法）在面试中常表现为什么？
q_en: How does training-data bias usually show up in an AI coding interview?
options: 给出教科书式解法，但不一定适合当前约束或代码库
遇到算法题会永远拒绝回答，什么也不生成
只能生成注释文字，完全不能生成任何代码
自动识别并精准套用每家公司的具体偏好
options_en: It gives a textbook solution that may not fit your specific constraints or codebase.
It will always refuse to answer any algorithm question and generate nothing.
It can only generate comment text and is completely unable to generate any code.
It automatically detects and precisely applies every company's specific preferences.
why: AI 可能给出技术上正确、策略上不合适的常见解法，你要判断它是否匹配题目约束和现有工具。
why_en: Training-data bias often gives a textbook solution that may not fit the specific constraints or codebase.

termDefinitions.meaning: AI 更容易给出训练语料里最常见的解法，而不一定是最贴合当前约束的解法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Training-data bias means the AI defaults to the most common solution in its training data, which may not fit your specific constraints.

optionExplanations: 常见解法技术上没错，但可能没用到代码库里更简单的现成方案。
误解：训练偏置指的是内容倾向，不是拒绝作答的行为。
误解：偏置和生成能力的形式无关，AI 照样能生成完整代码。
误解：AI 不会自动获得某家公司的具体偏好，这不是偏置的表现。
optionExplanations_en: The common answer is technically sound, but may skip a simpler option already available in the codebase.
Misconception: training bias is a content tendency, not a refusal to answer at all.
Misconception: bias has nothing to do with output form — the AI still generates full code.
Misconception: the AI gains no automatic awareness of a specific company's preferences from bias.

scenario: 面试还剩 15 分钟要口头讲清实现，AI 为一个 20 行的函数生成了 150 行多层抽象代码。
scenario_en: You have 15 minutes left and still have to walk through the code out loud, but the AI produced 150 lines with layers of abstraction for a 20-line function.
q: AI 输出过度冗长的主要代价是什么？
q_en: What is the main cost of overly verbose AI output?
options: 代码量越大就一定意味着越正确
面试官看到长代码一定会更喜欢
你需要理解、验证并解释更多不必要的抽象和注释
测试覆盖率会随着代码变长自动变全面
options_en: More code always necessarily means more correctness.
The interviewer will always end up liking longer code more.
You have to understand, verify, and defend more unnecessary abstractions and comments.
Test coverage automatically becomes more thorough simply because the code got longer.
why: 冗长代码增加审查面，也给面试官更多可追问但你未必能防守的内容。
why_en: Verbose output expands the surface you must understand, verify, and defend.
optionExplanations: 误解：行数和正确性没有必然关系，混淆了体量和质量。
误解：面试官通常更欣赏精简可控的输出，长度不是加分项。
每多一行都要能讲清楚它为什么在那，审查和答辩面被动放大。
误解：实现变长不会自动带来更全面的测试覆盖。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: line count has no necessary link to correctness — this conflates volume with quality.
Misconception: interviewers usually prefer concise, controlled output — length isn't a point-scorer.
Every extra line needs a reason you can explain on the spot, passively expanding what you must defend.
Misconception: a longer implementation doesn't automatically make test coverage more thorough.

scenario: 面试中你只让 AI 加一个 CSV 解析方法，它却顺手改动了类结构，而你要为每处改动辩护。
scenario_en: You only asked the AI to add one CSV parsing method, but it reshaped the class structure too — and you have to defend every change.
q: 哪些是 AI 常见的设计捷径或过度设计？（多选）
q_en: Which are common AI design shortcuts or over-designs? (Select all that apply.)
options: 为两个几乎无关的类创建 BaseProcessor
不必要地引入深继承层级
把简单 if-else 包成 strategy pattern
遵守现有最小接口
options_en: Create a BaseProcessor superclass for two barely related classes.
Introduce unnecessarily deep inheritance hierarchies.
Wrap a simple if-else in a strategy pattern.
Stick to the existing minimal interface.
why: 这些抽象可能不直接破坏功能，但会显得你接受了没有必要的设计复杂度。
why_en: Unneeded base classes, deep inheritance, and strategy wrappers can signal that you accepted lazy over-engineering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 示例中 AI 为两个几乎无关的类硬造出的公共父类，是过度抽象的典型产物。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BaseProcessor is the example of an unnecessary shared superclass the AI invents for two barely related classes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把可替换算法封装成独立类、通过接口切换的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The strategy pattern wraps interchangeable algorithms in separate classes swapped through a common interface.

optionExplanations: 挡不住风险：硬造的公共父类让以后改一个类容易牵连另一个不相关的类。
带来的压力：层级越深，定位一个方法实际生效在哪一层就越难。
带来的压力：模式复杂度超过分支本身，读者要多学一层结构才看懂逻辑。
不是过度设计：接口保持最小是应保留的克制，不需要新学任何结构。
optionExplanations_en: Risk it creates: a forced shared superclass lets a later change to one class accidentally ripple into the unrelated one.
Pressure it adds: the deeper the hierarchy, the harder it is to trace which layer a method actually runs in.
Pressure it adds: pattern complexity exceeds the branch it wraps, forcing readers to learn a layer just to see the logic.
Not over-design: keeping the interface minimal is the restraint worth keeping, nothing new to learn.

scenario: AI 说 bug 修好了、测试全绿，你看 diff 发现它同时动了测试文件和类型标注。
scenario_en: The AI says the bug is fixed and all tests are green, but the diff shows it also touched the test file and the type annotations.
q: 哪些 AI 生成行为属于严重的 correctness shortcut（掩盖而非修复真实错误的取巧做法）？（多选）
q_en: Which AI-generated behaviors are serious correctness shortcuts? (Select all that apply.)
options: 删除失败测试而不是修实现
用 any 绕过类型错误
吞掉异常或硬编码特定测试值
保留失败测试并定位根因
options_en: Delete a failing test instead of fixing the implementation.
Use `any` to bypass a type error.
Swallow exceptions or hardcode specific test values.
Keep the failing test and track down the root cause.
why: 这些做法让表面错误消失，但真实问题仍在，是面试官会追问的红旗。
why_en: Deleting tests, silencing types, or hardcoding values hides bugs instead of fixing them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为了让代码看起来通过，掩盖而非修复真实错误的取巧做法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A correctness shortcut is a trick that makes code look like it passes without actually fixing the underlying bug.

termDefinitions.meaning: TypeScript 中关闭类型检查的“万能类型”，用它能绕过编译期类型错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In TypeScript, `any` is the escape-hatch type that turns off compile-time type checking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 捕获异常的语法结构，如果 catch 块什么也不做就会把错误悄悄吞掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: try/catch is the exception-handling construct, and an empty catch block silently swallows the error.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把本该动态计算的值写死成固定值，通常只为让某个测试用例通过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hardcoding means baking in a fixed value that should be computed dynamically, often just to make one test pass.

optionExplanations: 挡不住风险：红灯变绿灯了，但底层 bug 原样留在实现里。
挡不住风险：类型系统失去保护，问题会拖到运行时才炸出来。
挡不住风险：错误被压制而不是修复，换一批输入立刻打回原形。
不是取巧：保留红灯去追根因，才是应对失败测试的正确做法。
optionExplanations_en: Risk it fails to block: the red light turns green while the underlying bug stays exactly where it was.
Risk it fails to block: the type system loses its protection until the bug surfaces at runtime instead.
Risk it fails to block: the error is suppressed rather than fixed, and resurfaces the moment inputs change.
Not a shortcut: leaving the test red and tracing the cause is the correct response to a failure.

scenario: AI 第一次输出偏离你的要求，没有使用你指定的数据结构。
scenario_en: The AI's first output drifted from your request and did not use the data structure you specified.
q: 这时最好的下一步是什么？
q_en: What is the best next step here?
options: 原样重复同一个提示，不加任何新信息
接受这次偏离，继续在上面叠功能
带更多上下文重新表述，明确必须使用的数据结构
马上切换模型，但完全不改提示内容
options_en: Repeat the exact same prompt again, adding no new information.
Accept this drift and keep layering new features on top of it.
Rephrase with more context, stating the required data structure explicitly.
Immediately switch models while leaving the prompt content completely unchanged.
why: 如果第一次没理解，重复原话通常不会改善；更清晰的上下文和约束才是有效修正。
why_en: If the AI missed the request, rephrase with clearer context and constraints rather than repeating the same prompt.
whenOtherWins: 如果偏离只是一个小局部且你能十秒改好，直接手修会更快。
tradeoff: 重提示一次的时间成本 vs 偏差累积的返工成本 —— 说清楚约束换取一次修正，好过在错误结构上继续堆功能。
codeSample:
Before: "Implement the cache eviction logic."
After: "Implement cache eviction using a doubly linked list + hash map
for O(1) LRU eviction, matching the existing Cache class fields."
optionExplanations: 没加新信息时，AI 第一次没理解的地方大概率还会同样理解错。
在已知偏差的结构上继续叠功能，返工成本会随时间放大。
补上数据结构等具体约束，是对因下药，最可能让输出对齐意图。
光换模型不改约束，没解决问题根源，还多花一份上下文重建成本。
optionExplanations_en: With no new information added, whatever the AI misunderstood the first time likely gets misunderstood again.
Building more features on a structure already known to be off just lets the rework cost grow over time.
Filling in the missing constraint, like the required data structure, targets the actual cause most directly.
Swapping models without touching the constraints skips the real fix and adds a context-rebuild cost on top.

scenario: 开放式面试 60 分钟，AI 连续三次生成把原本可运行的代码改坏，现在只剩 20 分钟。
scenario_en: In a 60-minute open-ended interview, three AI generations in a row broke code that used to run, and you're down to 20 minutes.
q: 开放式面试里为什么建议频繁提交或保留回滚点（代码可运行时的一次提交）？
q_en: Why keep frequent commits or rollback points during an open-ended interview?
options: 为了在面试官面前展示自己熟悉多少条 git 命令
因为面试系统里每提交一次代码都会自动加一次分
AI 连续跑偏时，回到上一个可运行状态通常比手工拆坏改动更快
为了图省事，正好可以借口避免再写测试
options_en: To show the interviewer how many git commands you know.
Because the interview system auto-adds points for every single commit.
When the AI drifts repeatedly, returning to the last working state is usually faster than manually undoing the damage.
As a convenient excuse to avoid writing tests.
why: 坏生成叠多了会很难局部修复，干净回滚点能保护你不被错误改动拖住。
why_en: Frequent checkpoints let you return to a working state when several bad AI generations pile up.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Good[Known good] --> Commit[Checkpoint]
  Commit --> Try[AI change]
  Try --> Bad{Bad path?}
  Bad -->|yes| Back[Rollback]
  Bad -->|no| Keep[Keep going]

termDefinitions.meaning: 代码处于已知可运行状态时的一次提交，可以随时退回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rollback point is a commit made while the code is in a known-working state that you can return to.

optionExplanations: 误解：回滚点的价值是恢复速度，不是拿来展示命令熟练度。
误解：分数不来自提交次数本身，这套自动加分机制并不存在。
AI 连续跑偏时，直接退回可运行状态，比逐处手工拆解改动快得多。
误解：回滚点和是否写测试是两件独立的事，不能拿来当借口。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: rollback points earn their value from recovery speed, not from showing off git commands.
Misconception: score doesn't come from commit count itself — no such auto-bonus mechanism exists.
When the AI drifts repeatedly, jumping back to a working state beats manually untangling each bad change.
Misconception: rollback points and writing tests are separate concerns, not an excuse to skip one for the other.

scenario: AI 生成的分页代码能跑，但它误解了排序需求，整体结构是照错误假设搭起来的。
scenario_en: The AI's pagination code runs, but it misread the sort requirement, so the whole structure is built on a wrong assumption.
q: AI 输出“90% 正确”时，为什么手工逐行补最后 10% 常常是陷阱？
q_en: Why is hand-patching the last 10% of a mostly-right AI output often a trap?
options: 因为面试规则里明确规定手写代码永远不被允许
因为 AI 会在你不知情时主动删除你后加的改动
你可能花更久修补混乱结构，不如用更清楚的提示重新生成
因为 90% 正确这个比例本身就已经一定足够上线
options_en: Because interview rules explicitly state that hand-writing code is never allowed.
Because the AI actively deletes your later edits without you knowing.
You may spend longer patching a confused structure than reprompting clearly for a clean regeneration.
Because a 90% correct ratio is, by itself, always already good enough to ship.
why: 半 AI 半手补的代码容易变乱，如果偏差来自误解需求，清晰重提示通常更快。
why_en: Patching a mostly-wrong output can be slower than reprompting clearly because the structure may already be misaligned.
optionExplanations: 误解：手写代码从来不是被禁止的选项，陷阱不是禁令问题。
误解：AI 不会主动删掉你后加的改动，风险不来自这个机制。
半 AI 半手改的结构越补越乱，重提示往往比逐处打补丁更省时间。
误解：剩下的 10% 常常正是边界情况，不能默认它已经够用。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: hand-writing code is never off-limits — the trap here isn't about a rule.
Misconception: the AI doesn't actively delete edits you add afterward — that's not where the risk comes from.
Half-AI, half-hand-edited structure gets messier the more you patch it; a clear reprompt is usually faster.
Misconception: the missing 10% is often exactly the edge case that can't be assumed already fine.

scenario: 你已经花两分钟让 AI 写对十行逻辑，但它连续两次没理解；你自己一分钟能写完。
scenario_en: You have spent two minutes trying to get AI to write ten lines, it missed twice, and you can write them in one minute.
q: 最务实的选择是什么？
q_en: What is the most pragmatic choice?
options: 继续和 AI 纠缠直到成功
换一个无关模型继续试
停止提示，自己写这十行
放弃这个功能
options_en: Keep fighting with the AI until it finally succeeds.
Switch to an unrelated model and keep trying.
Stop prompting and write the ten lines yourself.
Give up on the feature entirely.
why: 工具的目的不是证明能用 AI，而是更快正确推进；能手写更快时就该手写。
why_en: If writing it yourself is faster than fighting the AI, do that and keep moving.
whenOtherWins: 如果实现很长但只是约束表达不清，先做一次更具体的重提示仍可能划算。
tradeoff: 继续纠缠的时间成本 vs 自己写的确定性 —— 已知一分钟能搞定时，纠缠 AI 的边际时间不再划算。
optionExplanations: 已经两次没成功，继续纠缠只是追加沉没成本，收益不确定。
换模型有上下文重建成本，问题未必出在模型本身，不一定划算。
已知一分钟能写完，直接动手是总耗时最短的选择，工具是手段不是目的。
功能本身并不难，只因工具没配合就放弃，是不必要的损失。
optionExplanations_en: Two failed attempts already spent — continuing just chases sunk cost with uncertain payoff.
Switching models costs context-rebuild time, and the problem may not even be the model itself.
Knowing it takes one minute by hand makes writing it yourself the shortest total path — the tool is a means, not the goal.
The feature itself isn't hard; giving up just because the tool didn't cooperate is an unnecessary loss.

q: 补全一条经验规则：
q_en: Complete this rule of thumb:
text: 如果 AI 第一次没写对，可以{{重提示一次}}；如果仍没对，通常应该{{自己写}}或缩小任务，而不是继续耗时。
why: 单个生成上纠缠超过几分钟，往往比直接实现或拆小问题更不划算；这是给定的经验阈值，不是靠公式推导出来的。
why_en: A practical rule of thumb is one reprompt, then write it yourself or break the task down.

scenario: 面试平台给了两个可选模型，第一次输出偏离需求，你还剩 30 分钟且上下文都在当前会话里。
scenario_en: The platform offers two models, the first output missed the requirement, and you have 30 minutes left with all the context living in the current session.
q: 面试中 AI 输出不佳时，为什么切换模型通常不是首选？
q_en: When AI output is poor in an interview, why is switching models usually not the first move?
options: 切换模型这件事一定被平台规则禁止
切换模型这个动作会直接删除代码库
不同模型的输出质量其实完全一样
更具体地重提示或自己写，通常比切换上下文更快
options_en: Switching models is something the platform rules always forbid outright.
The act of switching models directly deletes the codebase.
Different models' output quality is in fact completely identical.
Reprompting more specifically or writing it yourself is usually faster than switching context.
why: 模型切换有上下文和时间成本，问题常常来自提示不清或任务太大，而不是模型名称。
why_en: Reprompting more specifically or writing it yourself is usually faster than switching models mid-interview.
tradeoff: 切换模型的上下文成本 vs 重提示/自己写的确定性 —— 换模型要重建上下文，通常比说清楚约束更慢。

termDefinitions.meaning: AI 助手在当前会话里已经了解的代码、约束和历史信息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Context is everything the AI assistant already knows in the current session — the code, constraints, and history so far.

optionExplanations: 误解：切换模型通常不是被禁止，只是时间上不划算。
误解：切换模型不会对代码库产生任何破坏性影响。
误解：不同模型的输出质量确实存在差异，不能一概而论。
重提示或自己写不需要重建上下文，通常比换模型更省时间。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: switching models usually isn't forbidden, it's just a bad time trade.
Misconception: switching models has no destructive effect on the codebase at all.
Misconception: output quality does differ across models — this can't be flattened to identical.
Reprompting or writing it yourself skips rebuilding context, usually saving time over a model switch.

scenario: 你平时用带仓库索引和自定义规则的 IDE 助手，面试却只能在平台自带的纯聊天框里写。
scenario_en: You normally use an IDE assistant with repo indexing and custom rules, but the interview only gives you the platform's plain chat box.
q: 结构化面试里的 AI 为什么可能感觉比你平时用的工具弱？
q_en: Why might AI in a structured interview feel weaker than your everyday tools?
options: 因为公司平台一定是故意把 AI 削弱来为难候选人，这是明确规则
因为面试用的浏览器在技术上无法运行任何模型调用
因为面试题目的文本内容根本传不进 AI 的输入窗口
因为平台 AI 可能缺少日常工具里的系统提示、代码上下文和工作流集成
options_en: Because the company platform must be deliberately weakening the AI to make it hard for candidates — that's an explicit rule.
Because the interview browser is technically incapable of running any model calls at all.
Because the interview problem's text content technically can never reach the AI's input window.
Because the platform AI may lack the system prompt, code context, and workflow integration your daily tools have.
why: 不管是否故意限制，实际效果是工具能力更弱，你需要降低期待并更多依赖自己的理解。
why_en: Interview AI may feel weaker because it lacks the system prompt, context, and workflow integration of your daily tools.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在用户看不到的地方预先设定 AI 行为和上下文的隐藏指令。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A system prompt is the hidden instruction that pre-configures an AI assistant’s behavior and context before the user’s own messages.

optionExplanations: 误解：是否故意本身不确定，把它断言成明确规则过于绝对。
误解：浏览器本身能正常承载模型调用，不是能力弱的原因。
误解：AI 通常能正常读到题目文本，这不是问题所在。
缺少系统提示、代码上下文和工作流集成，才是体感变弱的真正原因。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: whether it's deliberate is actually uncertain, so stating it as an explicit rule overreaches.
Misconception: a browser can carry model calls just fine — that's not what causes weaker capability.
Misconception: the AI can usually read the problem text without issue — that isn't the bottleneck.
Missing the system prompt, code context, and workflow integration is the real reason it feels weaker.

scenario: 面试平台的 AI 上下文很短、读不到整个仓库，你要在 45 分钟内完成一个 REST 接口。
scenario_en: The platform AI has a short context window and can't see the whole repo, and you have 45 minutes to finish a REST endpoint.
q: 遇到能力受限的面试 AI 时，适合让它做哪些事？（多选）
q_en: When interview AI is limited, what tasks are still good fits? (Select all that apply.)
options: 生成样板代码
解释陌生语法
搭建基础结构
替你做所有架构判断
options_en: Generate boilerplate code.
Explain unfamiliar syntax.
Scaffold basic structure.
Make every architecture decision for you.
why: 弱 AI 仍能加速基础工作，但难点思考和架构取舍必须由你兜住。
why_en: A limited AI can still help with boilerplate, syntax explanations, and scaffolding while you own the hard reasoning.
optionExplanations: 减掉的压力：重复模式代码交给它写，省下打字体量。
挡住的风险：语言/库用法卡壳时，靠它补齐知识空白而不是干等。
减掉的压力：先搭出骨架再填细节，起步更快，但骨架是否合理仍要你把关。
不该外包：架构取舍正是你该兜住的判断，能力受限时外包风险更高。
optionExplanations_en: Pressure it relieves: repetitive pattern code goes to it, saving typing volume.
Risk it blocks: when a syntax or library usage stalls you, it fills the knowledge gap instead of you guessing.
Pressure it relieves: a starter scaffold speeds up the beginning, though you still judge whether it's sound.
Not to outsource: architecture judgment is exactly what you must own, riskier still when the AI is limited.

scenario: 你只用最强的 IDE 助手练习，而目标公司的面试平台只给一个无仓库上下文的聊天框。
scenario_en: You've only ever practiced with your strongest IDE assistant, but the target company's platform gives you a chat box with no repo context.
q: 只用最强日常 AI 工具练习，面试时有什么风险？
q_en: What is the risk of practicing only with your strongest everyday AI tool?
options: 风险其实很小，因为不管哪个模型能力都完全一样
你会因为换了个工具就完全不会写提示了
所有结构化面试平台都会自动帮你同步日常工具的个人设置
你可能没有形成在受限 AI 只能完成一部分时继续推进的工作流
options_en: The risk is actually small because every model has exactly the same capability.
You would completely forget how to write a prompt just from switching tools.
Every structured interview platform automatically syncs your daily-tool personal settings.
You may never build a workflow for making progress when a limited AI can only get you part of the way.
why: 真实面试工具可能更慢、更弱或上下文更少，没练过受限环境会让你措手不及。
why_en: Practicing only with top-tier daily tools can leave you unprepared when interview AI is slower or less capable.
optionExplanations: 误解：不同模型能力差距是真实存在的风险，不能当成可忽略的量。
误解：换工具不会让提示能力彻底消失，这是夸大后果。
误解：结构化平台通常不会带你的个人配置，同步这件事并不存在。
真正缺的是受限工具只能完成一部分时，你怎么接着往下推进的套路。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: the capability gap between models is a real risk, not something safe to write off.
Misconception: switching tools doesn't wipe out your prompting ability — this overstates the consequence.
Misconception: structured platforms usually don't carry your personal config — no such sync exists.
What's actually missing is a playbook for pushing forward once a limited AI can only get you partway.

q: 把 AI 输出不佳时的恢复链排好：
q_en: Put the recovery chain for poor AI output in the correct order:
steps: 如果仍失败且手写更快，就自己实现
识别具体偏差：算法、接口、风格或正确性
用更具体的上下文和约束重提示一次
运行或审阅确认修正是否有效
why: 恢复坏输出要先定位偏差，再重定向，再验证；持续失败时果断脱离 AI。
why_en: Recover from bad output by identifying the mismatch, reprompting with constraints, verifying, then writing it yourself if needed.
tradeoff: 重提示一次 vs 直接接管 —— 先花一次精确重提示的成本，换取避免过早放弃 AI 的效率损失；反复失败就该换成本更低的自己写。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Bad[Bad output] --> Diagnose[Name issue]
  Diagnose --> Reprompt[One focused reprompt]
  Reprompt --> Review[Review result]
  Review --> Decide{Better?}
  Decide -->|no| Manual[Take over]

scenario: AI 建议用一个新架构，但你还无法解释它为什么比原计划更适合当前题目。
scenario_en: The AI suggests a new architecture, but you cannot yet explain why it fits this problem better than your original plan.
q: 你应该怎么做？
q_en: What should you do?
options: 马上采纳，因为 AI 可能更聪明
让 AI 自己决定所有后续步骤
删除原计划
先不采纳，除非你能说明它更适合的原因
options_en: Adopt it immediately because the AI might be smarter.
Let the AI decide every subsequent step on its own.
Delete the original plan outright.
Hold off unless you can explain why it actually fits better.
why: 改变方案的理由必须来自你对题目和约束的判断，而不是 AI 提出了一个看起来高级的替代品。
why_en: You should only adopt an AI-suggested approach if you can explain why it better fits the problem.
whenOtherWins: 如果 AI 指出了你确实漏掉的约束，并且新方案能清楚解决它，那就是合理的 pivot。
tradeoff: 方案切换的潜在收益 vs 你能否为它辩护 —— 换方案的理由必须来自你的判断，不是 AI 看起来更高级。
optionExplanations: 只因来源是 AI 就采纳，被追问原因时会答不上来。
决策权本该在你，整体外包后面试官看不到任何你自己的判断。
还没确认新方案站得住就先销毁旧方案，一旦不成立就没了退路。
把采纳门槛设在能不能自己说清原因，是能在追问下站住的判据。
optionExplanations_en: Adopting it just because it came from the AI leaves you stuck when asked to justify the switch.
This decision should still be yours — outsourcing it all shows the interviewer no judgment of your own.
Destroying the old plan before confirming the new one holds up leaves you no way back if it doesn't.
Setting the bar at being able to explain the reason yourself is what survives follow-up questioning.

scenario: 测试正红着，还剩 30 分钟两个功能没写，你想先让 AI 把下一个功能加上，回头一起修。
scenario_en: Tests are red, two features are still missing with 30 minutes left, and you want the AI to add the next feature first and fix everything later.
q: “不要在破损代码上继续叠新功能”背后的原因是什么？
q_en: Why should you avoid layering new features on top of broken code?
options: 因为破损代码上新功能一定完全写不出来
因为 AI 无法读取编译器给出的报错信息
因为面试官的规则不允许运行任何测试
你会失去错误来源，后续调试成本快速放大
options_en: Because new features simply cannot be written on broken code at all.
Because the AI is unable to read the error output the compiler gives.
Because the interviewer's rules do not allow running any tests.
You lose track of the error's source, and later debugging cost balloons.
why: 代码一旦处于未知坏状态，新错误和旧错误混在一起，AI 也更容易修错方向。
why_en: Layering features on broken code hides the source of errors and makes later debugging much more expensive.
optionExplanations: 误解：代码依然能继续写，只是新旧错误会叠加在一起。
误解：AI 通常能读到编译器报错，这不是限制的来源。
误解：运行测试通常是被鼓励的行为，不是被禁止的。
新旧错误交织在一起，回溯需要的排查时间会成倍增加。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: code can still be written on top, it's just that new and old errors stack together.
Misconception: the AI can usually read compiler error output fine — that's not the limiting factor.
Misconception: running tests is usually encouraged, not something interviewers forbid.
New and old errors tangle together, multiplying the time it takes to trace anything back.

scenario: AI 一次生成 80 行代码并宣称测试通过，你只有 3 分钟审阅就要向面试官解释它。
scenario_en: The AI dropped 80 lines in one shot and claims the tests pass; you get three minutes to review before explaining it to the interviewer.
q: 审阅 AI 输出时，应主动扫描哪些失败模式？（多选）
q_en: When reviewing AI output, which failure modes should you actively scan for? (Select all that apply.)
options: 是否换了你没同意的算法
是否引入不必要抽象
是否用类型或测试捷径掩盖问题
是否完全不需要运行
options_en: Whether it swapped in an algorithm you never approved.
Whether it introduced unnecessary abstractions.
Whether it used type or test shortcuts to hide problems.
Whether it means you never need to run the code at all.
why: 这些都是 AI 看似完成任务但实际偏离、过度设计或隐藏 bug 的常见方式。
why_en: Review AI output for unapproved algorithm changes, unnecessary abstractions, and shortcuts that hide bugs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 any 绕过类型检查、删测试或硬编码值等让代码表面通过的手法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A type or test shortcut is a trick — like using `any`, deleting tests, or hardcoding values — that makes code look correct on the surface.

optionExplanations: 挡住的风险：算法悄悄换了却没人发现，追问选择理由时答不上来。
挡住的风险：抽象层不知不觉膨胀，复杂度失控却没人察觉。
挡住的风险：any、空 catch、硬编码值让真实 bug 藏在看似通过的代码里。
误解：审阅不能替代实际运行，二者是互补关系不是替代关系。
optionExplanations_en: Risk it blocks: an algorithm swapped quietly leaves you unable to answer why it was chosen.
Risk it blocks: abstraction creeps in unnoticed and complexity spirals without anyone catching it.
Risk it blocks: `any`, empty catches, or hardcoded values let a real bug hide inside code that looks like it passes.
Misconception: review can never substitute for actually running the code — they're complementary, not interchangeable.

scenario: 45 分钟的面试里，AI 每次生成都吐出 150 行、带大段注释和额外抽象，而你每轮只有两三分钟审阅。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute interview the AI keeps returning 150 lines with long comments and extra abstractions, and you only get two or three minutes to review each round.
q: 压住 AI 输出体量最省事的手法是什么？
q_en: What is the cheapest way to keep AI output volume down?
options: 先接受长输出，生成完之后再让 AI 回头精简一遍
提示里直接加一句 "be concise"
把任务切到只剩几行的粒度，每次只让它写一小段
照单全收，自己手工删掉生成结果里的所有注释
options_en: Accept the long output first, then ask the AI to go back and trim it.
Add a plain "be concise" to the prompt itself.
Slice the task down to a few lines so it only writes a small chunk each time.
Take it all, then manually delete every comment from the generated result.
why: 审阅时间是这场面试的硬约束，控长指令把裁剪成本前置进提示，比生成后再精简少一整轮往返。代价：注释变少，关键决策得你口头补。
why_en: Reviewing time is the hard constraint here, so a short "be concise" in the prompt is cheaper than a whole extra round of trimming afterwards.
tradeoff: 输出体量 vs 自解释性 —— 短输出省下审阅和辩护时间，但代码里自带的说明也一起消失。
whenOtherWins: 如果这段代码要留给面试官事后阅读或交接给别人，保留说明性注释比压缩长度更值。

termDefinitions.meaning: 写进提示里的控长指令，要求 AI 只保留必要注释、不做解释性铺陈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: "Minimal comments" is a prompt instruction telling the AI to keep only essential comments instead of narrating the code.

optionExplanations: 误解：多花一轮往返做同一件事，而这轮时间正是面试里最缺的。
一句话前置约束（同理 "minimal comments"），同一轮就拿到短输出。
换个前提更好：逻辑很绕时切小粒度确实有用，但它控的是复杂度不是长度。
误解：注释删得掉，多余的抽象和额外分支删不掉，体量仍在。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: it spends an extra round on the same result, and that round is exactly what you lack.
One clause up front — "minimal comments" works the same — gets short output in the same round.
Wins under a different premise: fine-grained slicing helps for tricky logic, but it controls complexity, not length.
Misconception: you can delete comments, but not the extra abstractions and branches — the bulk stays.

scenario: 你日常工作里习惯凡事先问 AI 再动手，现在把同样节奏搬进面试，公司要判断你是用 AI 的工程师还是转发输出的传声筒。
scenario_en: At work you habitually ask the AI before doing anything, and now you bring that same rhythm into an interview where the company must judge whether you are an engineer using AI or just a relay forwarding its output.
q: 为什么日常那套"凡事先问 AI"在面试里要调整？
q_en: Why does the everyday habit of asking AI for everything need adjusting in an interview?
options: 面试平台会统计你的提示次数，超过阈值就直接扣分
面试环境每次 AI 调用都要排队，往返延迟显著更高
面试要看的是你的判断，全接受输出等于什么都没暴露
日常工作里频繁问 AI 其实也带着同等大小的下行风险
options_en: The platform counts your prompts and docks points once you pass a threshold.
Every AI call in the interview environment queues up, so round trips are far slower.
The interview is judging your reasoning, and accepting output wholesale reveals none of it.
Asking AI constantly at work actually carries an equally large downside risk.
why: 日常提示 AI 没有下行风险，而面试的产出除了代码还有你的思考过程，全盘转发会把这部分抹掉。代价：你得额外花时间把选择理由说出口。
why_en: At work there is no downside to asking the AI for everything, but in an interview the output includes your reasoning, and forwarding the AI wholesale erases it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只负责把需求转发给 AI、再把输出原样交出去、不对决策负责的候选人形象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A prompt relay is a candidate who just forwards requests to the AI and hands back its output without owning any of the decisions.

optionExplanations: 误解：没有这种计数扣分机制，被评估的是决策归属不是提示条数。
误解：调用延迟不是重点，就算瞬间返回问题也一样存在。
面试官只能从你的取舍里了解你，全盘接受就没有可评估的信号。
误解：日常场景恰恰相反，多问一次几乎零成本，这正是两种语境的差别。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: no such prompt-counting penalty exists; what is evaluated is who owns the decisions.
Misconception: call latency is beside the point — the problem persists even with instant replies.
Interviewers can only learn about you from your tradeoffs; accepting everything leaves no signal.
Misconception: day-to-day is the opposite — one more prompt costs almost nothing, and that is the difference.

scenario: 你刚让 AI 给 Dictionary 类加完 searchByPrefix，编译通过、现有测试全绿，而面试官已经十分钟没听到你说话了。
scenario_en: You just had the AI add searchByPrefix to the Dictionary class, it compiles and the existing tests are green, and the interviewer has not heard you speak for ten minutes.
q: 这个"编译加测试通过"的时刻最该被怎么用？
q_en: How should you use the moment when it compiles and tests pass?
options: 静默推进，等所有功能都做完再一次性汇报给面试官
趁状态干净，让 AI 一次性把剩下的功能全部生成出来
当作报进度的检查点：说清已验证什么、下一步做什么
回头把已通过的代码重构一遍，向面试官展示代码品味
options_en: Stay silent and report everything to the interviewer once all the features are done.
Use the clean state to have the AI generate all the remaining features in one shot.
Treat it as a checkpoint: say what is verified and what comes next.
Refactor the passing code to show the interviewer your taste in code.
why: 绿色构建是唯一无争议的进度事实，用它报进度比口头声称"快好了"可信得多。代价：每次开口会打断手上节奏几秒钟。
why_en: A green build is the one piece of progress nobody can dispute, so it is a far more credible thing to narrate than claiming you are almost done.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代码可运行且测试通过的那一刻，可以安全停下来汇报或回滚的稳定状态点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A checkpoint is the moment the code runs and tests pass, a stable state you can safely narrate from or roll back to.

optionExplanations: 误解：面试官需要沿途的信号，攒到最后汇报就没人知道你中间在想什么。
误解：一次生成多个功能会重新回到"堆叠未验证改动"的状态。
已验证的事实拿来报进度，面试官同步了你的位置，你也确认了落点。
换个前提更好：代码明显难维护时值得重构，但此刻功能还没做完，时间更紧。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: the interviewer needs signal along the way; saving it all for the end hides your thinking.
Misconception: generating several features at once puts you right back into stacked, unverified changes.
A verified fact makes the progress report land: the interviewer syncs to where you are and you confirm your footing.
Wins under a different premise: refactoring pays when the code is clearly unmaintainable, but features are still unfinished here.

scenario: 面试平台自带的 AI 里，你贴上一段有越界 bug 的代码问它有没有问题，它只回了一句"注意检查边界条件"。
scenario_en: You paste code with an out-of-bounds bug into the interview platform AI and ask what is wrong, and it only answers "watch your boundary conditions".
q: 受限的面试 AI 常见的具体症状有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are the typical symptoms of a limited interview AI? (Select all that apply.)
options: 不直接指出 bug，只给方向性提示
回答含糊或明显不完整
对某些类型的请求直接拒绝
生成的代码总是连编译都过不了
options_en: It hints at a direction instead of naming the bug outright.
It answers vaguely or leaves the answer clearly incomplete.
It flatly refuses certain categories of request.
The code it generates never even compiles.
why: 这三种症状说明工具能力被限，而不是你提示写错；认出来才能及时把难点思考收回自己手上。代价：你要多花时间自己推理。
why_en: These symptoms mean the tool is limited rather than your prompt being wrong, so you can stop rewording and take the hard reasoning back yourself.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试环境里体感明显弱于日常工具的 AI，多因缺少系统提示与代码上下文而非被刻意削弱。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A "nerfed" AI is one that feels noticeably weaker in an interview, usually because it lacks the system prompt and code context of your daily tools.

optionExplanations: 识别信号：Uber 候选人形容它只给 nudge，你别再反复改措辞求它点破。
识别信号：答案缺片段时应停止追问，改用它做样板代码这类稳妥活。
识别信号：撞到拒答就换任务类型，别把时间烧在绕过限制上。
误解：文章没有这一条，受限 AI 的输出通常仍能编译，只是不够到位。
optionExplanations_en: Signal to catch: Uber candidates describe it as giving nudges — stop rewording in hopes it names the bug.
Signal to catch: when answers come back partial, switch it to safe work like boilerplate instead of pressing.
Signal to catch: on a refusal, change the kind of task rather than burning time routing around it.
Misconception: the article claims no such thing — limited AI output usually still compiles, it is just unhelpful.
